theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: Before dinner service, why does the villa manager hold a short briefing with the service staff?
options: To decide which of the staff can go home early tonight
To share the menu, specials and any guest allergies
To count and share out the tips from the night before
To plan the staff's days off for the coming month

The cloth that is spread over the whole table
The lid placed over a hot dish to keep it warm

On the left, with the cutting edge facing out

options: On the left, next to the side plate
In the middle of the cover, on the plate
Above the tip of the main knife

questions.stem: Where does the side plate (bread plate) go in a standard cover?
options: On the right of the knives
In the centre, on the napkin
Above the glasses, at the back

options: Knife and fork placed together on the plate
Knife and fork crossed in the middle of the plate

The plate pushed to the middle of the table

options: The water glasses and the guests' napkins

options: Pick it up, wipe it on your cloth and give it back

options: Put out a wet-floor sign and wipe it up straight away

options: Held out at arm's length, so nothing spills on you
Tilted towards you, so you can see every item on it
Close to the body, with the heaviest items in the centre
In one hand, with the heaviest items near the edge

options: Say no and walk away, since there is nothing you can do

questions.stem: A family with a small child comes to dinner. Which is a helpful thing to do?
options: Seat the family by the kitchen door, away from the others

questions.stem: A guest says the fish is cold. What should you do first?
options: Apologise, take the plate and ask the kitchen for a hot one

Explain that the cook is very busy and has a lot to do tonight
Leave the plate and quietly take it off the bill at the end

questions.stem: Why should you tell your supervisor about a guest complaint, even after you have solved it?
options: So the supervisor can blame the person who caused it
So the guest can be charged extra for the trouble
So it is recorded and can be stopped from happening again
So the complaint can be kept hidden from the villa owner

questions.stem: Guests are in a private conversation when their food is ready. What should you do?
options: Speak loudly over them so they know the food is here
Wait for a pause, then serve quietly with "excuse me"

questions.stem: How should you present the bill when a guest asks for it?
options: Read the total aloud from across the room
Bring it with the main course, so they can pay early
Hand it to the youngest guest at the table

questions.stem: A guest wants to pay a J$ bill in US$. Which exchange rate should you use?
options: The rate the villa manager has set for that day
Any rate the guest says is fair to them

questions.stem: Before you give the bill to the guest, what should you check?
options: That a tip has already been added in for you
That the guest's room number is in large print
That every item ordered is on it and the total is right
That the bill shows what each dish cost the kitchen

questions.stem: A guest pays a J$4,000 bill with a J$5,000 note. How much change is due?
At the end of service, what should you do with the bottles of sauce and other condiments?
options: Leave them out on the tables, ready for breakfast
Wipe them, close them and store them as the house rules say
Pour them together into one bottle to save space
Throw them all away every night, even if nearly full

questions.stem: Why do you restock the service station before your shift ends?
options: So the next shift has what it needs to start service
So the manager thinks you stayed late that night
So you can take any spare items home with you
So that guests can help themselves to cutlery

questions.stem: Where should dirty table linen go after service?
options: Shaken out over the terrace and folded for tomorrow
On the kitchen counter, next to the clean plates
Into the linen bag or hamper, away from food

questions.stem: Which is right for a server's appearance at the villa?
options: Strong perfume, so that the guests notice you as you pass

essays.stem: Describe how you would prepare the dining area and the service station before dinner service at a villa.
essays.modelAnswer: About an hour before service I would check the booking: how many guests, the time, any special requests and any allergies, and I would go to the briefing to learn the menu and the specials. I would make sure the dining area is clean, the floor swept and dry, and the lights, fans and music set. I would lay clean tablecloths and napkins, and set each cover with polished cutlery and glasses, holding them by the handle or stem. I would check that the chairs are clean and steady, and put salt, pepper and a small flower arrangement on the table. At the service station I would stock spare cutlery, napkins, glasses, side plates, trays, service cloths, order pads, menus, water jugs, ice and condiments. Last, I would check my own uniform and grooming and walk round once more to see that everything is ready.
markingPoints: Checks the booking, guest numbers and allergies, and attends the briefing
Makes sure the dining area is clean, safe and comfortable
Lays the tables neatly and hygienically, holding cutlery and glasses correctly
Stocks the service station with everything needed
Checks own grooming and makes a final check of the area

essays.stem: Describe how to lay a standard cover for a three-course dinner of soup, main course and dessert, and say how you check that the table is ready.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with a clean, ironed tablecloth, laid straight with an even drop on each side. For each guest I place a folded napkin in the centre of the cover. The main knife goes on the right with the cutting edge facing in, and the soup spoon goes to the right of the knife, because cutlery is used from the outside in. The main fork goes on the left. The dessert spoon and fork go above the cover, with the spoon handle pointing right and the fork handle pointing left. The side plate goes on the left of the fork, with the side knife on it. The water glass goes above the tip of the main knife, with a wine glass beside it if wine is served. Cutlery sits about a thumb's width from the table edge. To check, I stand back and look along the table: every cover should match and be in line, and every item clean, polished and not chipped.
markingPoints: Clean tablecloth laid straight with an even drop
Main knife on the right, edge in, with the soup spoon outside it (outside-in order)
Main fork on the left; dessert spoon and fork above the cover, handles the right way
Side plate and side knife on the left; water glass above the tip of the main knife
Checks that covers match, are in line, and that items are clean and not chipped

essays.stem: Describe the steps of greeting guests and taking their food and drink orders, from the moment they arrive to sending the order to the kitchen.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guests arrive I greet them with a smile, welcome them by name if I know it, and show them to their table, helping with chairs. I offer water and the menus, and tell them about the specials and anything that is not available tonight. I give them time to read the menu, and watch for the sign that they are ready. I ask whether anyone has an allergy or a special diet. I take the drinks order first, then the food order, usually ending with the host, and I write a seat number beside each item. I answer questions about the dishes honestly and suggest drinks or side dishes that go well with their choices. Then I repeat the order back to check it is right, thank the guests, and pass the order to the kitchen straight away, clearly written, with any allergy marked.
markingPoints: Greets warmly, welcomes and seats the guests
Offers water and menus and explains the specials
Asks about allergies and special diets
Takes drinks then food orders with seat numbers, answering questions and suggesting items
Repeats the order back and sends it to the kitchen promptly, with allergies marked

essays.stem: Explain how to serve and clear plated food safely and politely.
essays.modelAnswer: Before I carry plates out I check each one against the order: the right dish, the right temperature, a clean rim, and any allergy plate clearly marked. I hold plates by the rim, keeping my thumb off the food, and carry only as many as I can hold safely, using a service cloth for hot plates and warning the guest that the plate is hot. I serve each guest without asking who ordered what, by using the seat numbers, and place the plate with the main item nearest the guest. I follow the house style for the side I serve from, move quietly round the table, and never reach across a guest. I clear only when all the guests at the table have finished, shown by the knife and fork placed together on the plate. I ask if they enjoyed the meal, clear quietly, usually from the guest's right, taking the cutlery with the plate, and scrape and stack away from the table, never in front of guests.
markingPoints: Checks each plate against the order (dish, temperature, clean rim, allergy)
Carries plates safely by the rim, uses a service cloth and warns of hot plates
Serves by seat number with the main item nearest the guest, without reaching across
Clears only when all have finished (knife and fork together)
Clears quietly, scraping and stacking away from the guests

essays.stem: Describe how to serve a bottle of wine to a table of guests.
essays.modelAnswer: First I bring the bottle to the host and show the label, saying the name of the wine, so the host can confirm it is the wine ordered. White and sparkling wines are kept chilled in an ice bucket; red wine is served cool, not warm. I open the bottle at the table: I cut the foil below the lip, wipe the top, draw the cork gently with a corkscrew, and check the cork. I pour a small taste for the host. When the host is happy, I pour for the other guests from their right, and serve the host last. Each glass is poured about a third to half full, and at the end of each pour I give the bottle a small turn to stop drips and wipe the neck with my service cloth. I place the bottle in the bucket or on the table as the house style says, and top up glasses when they are low, never filling them more than half.
markingPoints: Presents the bottle to the host and confirms the label
Serves the wine at the right temperature (white chilled, red cool)
Opens the bottle neatly at the table and lets the host taste first
Pours from the guest's right, host last, about a third to half full
Prevents drips and tops up glasses during the meal

essays.stem: Explain why staff must serve alcohol responsibly, and describe what you would do if a guest has had too much to drink.
essays.modelAnswer: Alcohol affects judgement, balance and health. A guest who drinks too much may fall, get into danger in the pool or the sea, start a fight, or drive and crash, and the business can be blamed and get into trouble with the law. It is also against the law to sell alcohol to anyone under 18, so staff should ask for ID if a guest looks young. Responsible service means watching how much guests drink, offering water and food, and suggesting drinks without alcohol. If a guest has had too much, I would speak to them politely and quietly, away from others, and explain that I cannot serve more alcohol, but I can offer water, coffee or a soft drink. I would not argue with them or shame them. I would tell my supervisor, ask their friends to help, keep them away from the pool, make sure they do not drive, and write a note in the log.
markingPoints: Explains the risks to the guest and to the business
No alcohol to anyone under 18; checks ID when in doubt
Watches drinking, offers water, food and drinks without alcohol
Refuses further alcohol politely and privately, without arguing
Tells the supervisor, keeps the guest safe (pool, driving) and records it

essays.stem: A guest complains that their steak is overcooked. Describe how you would handle the complaint.
essays.modelAnswer: I would listen to the guest without interrupting, look at them and show that I care about the problem. I would apologise sincerely, for example: "I am very sorry the steak is not how you asked for it." I would not argue, make excuses or blame the kitchen in front of the guest. I would offer to put it right at once: a new steak cooked the way the guest wants it, or another dish if they prefer, and I would ask how they would like it cooked. I would take the plate away, tell the kitchen clearly what is needed, and tell my supervisor. While the new steak is cooking I would check the guest's drinks and look after the rest of the table. When I bring the new dish I check that it is right and that the guest is happy. After service I make sure the complaint is written down, so the team can learn from it.
markingPoints: Listens fully without interrupting
Apologises sincerely, without excuses or blame
Offers a remedy and acts quickly (new steak or another dish)
Tells the kitchen and the supervisor
Checks the guest is happy afterwards, and the complaint is recorded

essays.stem: Explain how you would serve a guest with a food allergy and a guest who uses a wheelchair, so that both enjoy the meal safely.
essays.modelAnswer: For the guest with a food allergy, I would ask exactly what they cannot eat and how serious it is, write it clearly on the order, and tell the cook and my supervisor. I would check the ingredients with the kitchen and never guess. I would carry their plate on its own, check it against the order, and serve it first so it is not mixed up with other plates. For the guest who uses a wheelchair, I would make sure the path to the table is clear, with no loose mats or steps where possible, and offer a table with room for the wheelchair, taking away a chair if they wish. I would ask how I can help instead of assuming, speak to the guest directly and not only to their companion, and place items within easy reach. Both guests should get the same warmth and respect as every other guest.
markingPoints: Allergy: asks, records clearly and tells the kitchen and supervisor
Allergy: checks ingredients, never guesses, serves the plate separately
Wheelchair: clear route and a table with room, chair removed if wanted
Asks how to help and speaks directly to the guest
Gives both guests the same warmth and respect

essays.stem: Describe how to prepare and present a bill and take payment, including payment in US dollars.
essays.modelAnswer: When the guest asks for the bill, I check it against the orders: every item is there, nothing extra, the prices are right, GCT is added at the current rate and the total adds up. I bring it in a clean folder, place it face down near the person who asked, and step back so they can check it in private. For cash, I count the money in front of the guest, say the amount received, and bring back the right change with a receipt. If the guest pays in US$, I use only the exchange rate the villa or manager has set for that day, work out the amount, tell the guest, and give change as the house rules say. For a card, I follow the steps on the card machine and do not take the card out of the guest's sight. At a villa, charges may go to the guest's account instead, so I ask the guest to check and sign the slip. I thank the guests warmly.
markingPoints: Checks the bill is accurate, with GCT at the current rate
Presents it discreetly in a folder
Counts cash in front of the guest and gives correct change and a receipt
Uses only the exchange rate set by the villa for US$
Handles card or account charges securely and thanks the guest

essays.stem: Describe the steps of closing down the dining area after dinner service, and say why each one matters.
essays.modelAnswer: When the last guests have left, I clear all the tables, carrying plates, glasses and cutlery to the wash-up area with care so nothing breaks. I wipe the condiment bottles, close them and store them as the house rules say, and put leftover bread and butter away or throw them out, so food stays safe. I take off the dirty linen and put it in the linen bag, away from food. I clean and sanitise the tables and chairs, then sweep and mop the floor with a wet-floor sign out, so nobody slips. I restock the service station with clean cutlery, glasses, napkins and menus, so the next shift can start quickly. I switch off the lights, fans and coffee machine to save power and prevent fires, lock away any alcohol and cash as the rules say, and report any breakages or low stock to my supervisor.
markingPoints: Clears tables and carries items safely to the wash-up
Stores condiments and leftover food safely; dirty linen into the linen bag
Cleans and sanitises furniture and mops with a wet-floor sign
Restocks the service station for the next shift
Switches off equipment, secures alcohol and cash, and reports breakages or low stock

practical1.title: Set a villa dining table and serve a three-course plated dinner to four guests
practical1.brief: Your group is the dining team for a villa dinner for four guests (the assessor and other trainees play the guests; the kitchen class or the Centre supplies simple food, or the group uses dummy dishes). Set the table with standard covers for soup, main course and dessert, and stock a service station. Then greet and seat the guests, take the drinks and food orders (one guest has a food allergy, which the assessor gives you), and serve and clear each course. Share the work so that every member lays at least one cover, takes at least one order, and serves and clears at least one course while the assessor watches. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the dining area is closed down.
materials: A dining table and 4 chairs, a tablecloth and 4 napkins
Cutlery for 4 covers: soup spoons, main knives and forks, dessert spoons and forks, side knives
Side plates, water and wine glasses, soup bowls, dinner plates and dessert plates
Trays, service cloths, a water jug, salt and pepper, and a small table flower
Food for three courses from the kitchen (or dummy dishes), and drinks without alcohol
Cleaning cloths, sanitiser and a wet-floor sign
photos: The service station stocked before service
The table laid with four standard covers, seen from above
A member taking an order, with the order pad showing seat numbers and the allergy
A member carrying plates correctly by the rim
The main course placed for each guest
The table crumbed down and set for dessert
The dining area closed down and the station restocked
checklist: Was well groomed, in clean uniform, and washed hands before handling cutlery and food
Laid a cover correctly: knife edge in, fork on the left, dessert cutlery above, side plate on the left, glass above the knife
Greeted and seated guests politely and offered water and menus
Took an order with seat numbers, asked about allergies and repeated it back
Carried and served plates safely by seat number, without reaching across guests
Cleared only when the guests had finished, quietly and safely
Handled the guest with the allergy correctly, checking with the kitchen
Took part in closing down and restocking the station
safety: Carry only as many plates as you can hold safely; use a service cloth for hot plates and warn guests
Wipe any spill at once and put out a wet-floor sign
Check glasses and plates for chips and cracks, and take any damaged item out of use
Keep the allergy plate apart and check it against the order before serving
Follow the Centre's rules for hygiene and for lifting tables and chairs

practical2.title: Set up and run a villa breakfast buffet with beverage service, and handle a guest complaint
practical2.brief: Your group sets up and runs a breakfast buffet for six villa guests (the assessor and other trainees play the guests). Lay out the buffet table with labelled dishes (with allergy notes), a serving tool for each dish, plates and cutlery, and set up a beverage area for juice, coffee and Jamaican chocolate tea. During service, keep the buffet full, tidy and at the right temperature, serve hot drinks to the tables, and clear as guests finish. Part-way through, the assessor makes a complaint (for example, that the coffee is cold or a dish has run out): one member handles it and fills in the complaint notes while the others keep the service going. Share the work so that every member sets up part of the buffet, serves at least one drink, and takes a turn in each role (buffet, beverages, clearing). Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group when the area is cleared and clean.
materials: Platters, bowls, serving spoons and tongs, and a chafing dish or hot-holding unit if the Centre has one
Breakfast food from the kitchen class, or fruit, bread, pastries and cereals
Small labels for each dish, with allergy notes
Juice jugs, a coffee pot, hot water, cocoa balls or chocolate, milk and sugar
Plates, bowls, cutlery, cups, saucers, glasses and napkins
Trays, service cloths, cleaning cloths, sanitiser and a wet-floor sign
photos: The buffet table laid out and labelled before the guests arrive
A member refilling or tidying the buffet during service
A member serving a hot drink to a seated guest
The complaint role play, with the member listening to the guest
The complaint notes sheet filled in
The buffet cleared and the area clean
checklist: Was well groomed and washed hands before handling food and service items
Laid out dishes neatly, with labels, allergy notes and a serving tool for each dish
Kept food covered and at the right temperature, and refilled dishes before they ran out
Served hot drinks safely from the guest's right, with the cup handle turned for the guest
Cleared tables quietly when guests had finished
Handled the complaint (listened, apologised, put it right, told the supervisor) or supported the member who did
Took part in clearing, storing leftovers safely and cleaning the area
safety: Keep hot food at about 63 °C or above and cold food at 5 °C or below, or as the Centre's food safety plan says
Give each dish its own serving tool, so allergens are not passed from one dish to another
Take care with hot water, coffee pots and chafing-dish heaters; follow the maker's instructions
Wipe spills at once and put out a wet-floor sign
Follow the Centre's rules for hygiene and for lifting tables
